feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with strong responsibility growth and domain consistency.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms, scale, and tools (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).  
- Writing is clear and audience-appropriate, with a strong strategic positioning in the summary and competencies.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; this repetition weakens structure and makes the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; keep comma style consistent in lists (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more concise opening, stronger results-oriented phrasing, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven, advocacy, or membership organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with more concrete value language such as “leading cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and editorial operations.”
- Tighten the final sentence to highlight a distinctive strength: translating policy/technical issues into accessible content for diverse stakeholders.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also appears elsewhere; avoid listing it prominently here unless paired with a specific differentiator.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve scanability; suggested version:
  Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Use parallel noun-based phrasing throughout for consistency.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority item to keep the list tighter and more executive-level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” overlaps with the header and Topline Skills (“Multi-channel communications leadership”).
- “Workflow & systems architecture” and “Editorial workflow design” are close enough that they may feel repetitive.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground outcomes, and avoid repeating themes already covered in the header, skills, and project section.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opener with a sharper scope statement: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built cross-functional content workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more outcome-driven: mention scale, speed, reuse, or stakeholder benefit if possible, e.g. “Created modular microsites, storytelling components, and member toolkits in Drupal to accelerate campaign launches and improve content reuse.”
- Keep the AI search bullet, but quantify or clarify value if possible: “Led AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.
- Governance/analytics/workflow language overlaps with the header and NACo role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if each bullet highlighted outcomes, not just responsibilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with: “Directed enterprise digital communications strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign support metrics if available; otherwise condense.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets: “Built reporting and decision-support infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the earlier NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep it here only if framed as org-level capacity building.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more role-specific by emphasizing operational leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to show scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging ahead of promotion to Director of Digital Media.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” echo the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/ownership, not creation alone.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme fit, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise-level leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social and video
- Public-sector advocacy messaging and audience-centered content strategy
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect leadership scope.
- Add “web modernization” to align with the most recent/highest-impact work.
- Keep each line distinct from tools/platform skills listed elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of separate platform names.
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Trim lower-signal or older items already covered elsewhere, especially jQuery and possibly WordPress/SharePoint unless target roles require them.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so vary wording or keep it in only one place.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.:
- Analytics infrastructure & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis
- Put the highest-value capability first: lead with “analytics infrastructure,” “KPI framework design,” or “executive reporting” rather than GA4.
- Standardize phrasing for seniority and clarity: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Leadership dashboards.”
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented modifier tied to recent work, such as “for enterprise web performance and content decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, distinctive, and tied to delivery scope rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability statement, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of generic terms: “livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy, conferences, and recurring executive content.”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to sound more senior.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Multimedia, Studio & Event Production” for clearer differentiation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in NACo experience, so this section should summarize specialization, not restate duties.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint; GitHub Pages last or remove if only lightly used.
- Consider adding level/context instead of just names, e.g., “Drupal 10, enterprise publishing” if accurate.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use “Microsoft Power Pages” rather than “Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider removing one version or making this one more implementation-focused.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same undifferentiated list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it sharper by emphasizing implementation depth and tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/outcome signals instead of pure tools, e.g. “front-end implementation for Drupal microsites,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (HTML5/CSS3) unless required; they add little senior-level value

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” and broader technical execution themes
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this category focused strictly on development tools

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Drop Basecamp unless it was meaningfully used in recent roles; it feels dated versus your current enterprise/public-sector profile.
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a pure list: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier (workflow automation/integrations) • Jira, Asana, Trello (project tracking) • Slack, Microsoft Teams (team coordination)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Slack/Teams are lower-value than your more distinctive technical tools, so keep this section concise.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant, but it reads as a bare tool list and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent roles. Make it sharper and aligned to enterprise email operations rather than generic “engagement.”

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email, newsletter and member communications platforms)**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses: **used to manage high-volume newsletters, campaign sends and audience communications**
- Keep only the strongest/current platforms; if Dynamics 365 was limited exposure, move it later or drop it in favor of the systems most central to NACo/freelance work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat outcomes here unless adding platform-specific context
- “Engagement” is vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications operations” language in Core Competencies

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads more like setup than impact. Since newer NACo roles already cover strategy/operations, this entry should emphasize foundational team-building, production execution, and any concrete scale/results.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social, video, and livestream production.”
- Split the second sentence into outcome-focused bullets or clauses; add metrics if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams, cadence/views of weekly videos, team size, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific outputs like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy video updates, and multimedia web content.”
- Clarify supervision: “mentored a digital media associate” or “provided day-to-day oversight to 1 digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the format, not scaling it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” risks repeating later operations language; frame this as early infrastructure-building.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope so it feels distinct from the later digital/media roles at NACo.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrases like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer business value: what programs, stakeholders, or outputs were supported?
- Split into 2 concise bullets and emphasize ownership:
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.
- Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy communications; produced digital and multimedia content to extend program visibility.
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences reached, projects supported, or teams/programs served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/program support.
- Avoid broad “digital communications” language here since stronger, more recent entries already cover that.
